title: The Italian Renaissance
description: Harmony, perspective, and humanism from the rebirth of classical ideals.
source: Art Institute of Chicago, The Metropolitan Museum of Art

items.title: Virgin and Child with an Angel
items.description_narrative: Sandro Botticelli's 'Virgin and Child with an Angel' is a delicate tempera on panel painting created between 1475 and 1485. It depicts a tender moment between the Virgin Mary, the Christ Child, and a watchful angel.
items.tags: religious art, renaissance, italian, madonna, sacred, serene, tempera painting

items.title: Virgin and Child with Two Angels
items.description_narrative: Sandro Botticelli's "Virgin and Child with Two Angels" depicts Mary tenderly holding the infant Christ, accompanied by two celestial figures. This tempera on panel artwork showcases the delicate forms and devotional sentiment characteristic of the artist's Florentine Renaissance style.
items.tags: religious art, renaissance, virgin and child, tempera, florentine, devotional, serene, italian art

items.title: Portrait Bust of a Young Man
items.medium: Brush and brown ink and brown and gray wash, over traces of graphite, on ivory wove paper, tipped on to tan laid paper with gray fibers
items.description_narrative: This drawing, a 'Portrait Bust of a Young Man,' showcases the delicate rendering typical of Sandro Botticelli's figurative works. Executed with brush and brown ink and washes, it captures a refined profile on ivory wove paper.
items.tags: portrait, bust, drawing, ink, renaissance, italian, male, profile, study

items.title: Self-Portrait
items.description_narrative: This striking 1878 oil on canvas captures artist Walter Shirlaw in a moment of self-reflection. The artwork serves as a direct visual record of the artist, rendered by his own hand.
items.tags: self-portrait, portrait, oil painting, american art, realism, 19th century, artist

items.title: Martin Vanden Bogaert Desjardins
items.medium: Engraving and etching on cream wove paper
items.description_narrative: Gérard Edelinck masterfully rendered this detailed portrait of Martin Vanden Bogaert Desjardins through engraving and etching. The artwork showcases the refined lines and tonal contrasts characteristic of the period's printmaking.
items.tags: portrait, engraving, etching, french art, baroque, 17th century, academic

items.title: Remembrance of Italy
items.description_narrative: Jean-Baptiste Camille Corot's 'Remembrance of Italy' is an etching on tan laid paper, crafted around 1866. This work reflects the artist's enduring connection to the Italian landscape, often revisited through memory and artistic expression.
items.tags: landscape, etching, printmaking, pastoral, 19th century, French art, memory, tranquil

items.title: A Sunday on La Grande Jatte — 1884
items.description_narrative: Georges Seurat's monumental oil on canvas, "A Sunday on La Grande Jatte — 1884," captures Parisians enjoying a leisurely afternoon on an island in the Seine. This iconic work is meticulously composed using the artist's groundbreaking pointillist technique, creating luminous color and form.
items.tags: sunday, leisure, park, pointillism, post-impressionism, Parisian life, serene, vibrant

items.title: Fishing Craft near the Cliffs at Collioure
items.medium: Etching on China paper colle laid down on white wove paper
items.description_narrative: This etching by Adolphe Appian captures fishing vessels navigating the dramatic coastline near Collioure, France. The intricate lines of the print convey the rugged texture of the cliffs and the dynamic movement of the sea.
items.tags: seascape, etching, fishing, collioure, coastline, 19th century, maritime

items.title: Interior of St. Mark's, Venice
items.description_narrative: This oil on canvas depicts the grand interior of St. Mark's Basilica in Venice, capturing its architectural details and atmosphere. Painted by David Dalhoff Neal in 1869, the work reflects a meticulous study of the historic Italian landmark.
items.tags: interior, church, venice, architectural, oil painting, 19th century, american art, realism

items.title: The Fall of the Giants
items.medium: Etching with drypoint in black on ivory laid paper
items.description_narrative: This etching with drypoint by Salvator Rosa vividly depicts the mythological Fall of the Giants. Created in 1663, the work utilizes intricate printmaking techniques on ivory laid paper to render the dramatic scene.
items.tags: mythology, giants, baroque, etching, drypoint, italian, printmaking, dramatic

items.title: It Rocks but is Not Sunk
items.description_narrative: This etching by Charles Meryon, created in 1854, depicts a scene evocative of its title, 'It Rocks but is Not Sunk.' It showcases Meryon's masterful use of the etching medium on ivory laid paper.
items.tags: etching, cityscape, printmaking, 19th century, urban, dramatic

items.title: Souvenir of Tuscany
items.description_narrative: This etching by Jean-Baptiste-Camille Corot captures a memento of his travels through Tuscany, rendered with the nuanced tonal qualities characteristic of the artist's printmaking. The delicate lines on ivory laid paper evoke the serene beauty of the Italian landscape, reflecting Corot's early explorations in print.
items.tags: landscape, etching, 19th century, french art, romanticism, nature, printmaking

items.title: Portrait of Edouard Molé
items.description_narrative: Robert Nanteuil's masterful engraving presents Edouard Molé, capturing his dignified presence with meticulous detail. Created in 1653, it exemplifies the precision and depth achievable through the printmaking technique on paper.
items.tags: portrait, man, engraving, baroque, 17th century, formal, realistic

items.title: View of Ponte Lugano on the Anio, from Views of Rome
items.medium: Etching on heavy ivory laid paper
items.description_narrative: This etching by Giovanni Battista Piranesi captures a dramatic 'View of Ponte Lugano on the Anio,' offering a glimpse into ancient structures within the Roman landscape. Created in 1763, this work on heavy ivory laid paper showcases Piranesi's masterful printmaking technique and his fascination with Rome's architectural grandeur.
items.tags: etching, architectural view, italian art, 18th century, landscape, roman ruins, printmaking

items.title: Tassels
items.description_narrative: These 'Tassels' originate from the Nasca culture, which flourished between 500 and 900 CE. While their specific use remains a subject of study, such objects often held symbolic or ceremonial importance within Nasca society.
items.tags: nasca, pre-columbian, south american, ancient, decorative object, ceremonial, artifact

items.title: Allegory of Venus and Cupid
items.description_narrative: This oil on canvas, titled "Allegory of Venus and Cupid," depicts classical mythological figures associated with love and desire. Created around 1600 by an imitator of Titian, it reflects themes popular in Renaissance Venetian art.
items.tags: mythology, allegory, classical, renaissance, venetian, love, oil painting, human figures

items.title: Tobias and the Angel
items.medium: Pen and black ink, with brush and gray wash, on ivory laid paper
items.description_narrative: Titian's 'Tobias and the Angel' depicts the biblical story of Tobias guided by the Archangel Raphael, a theme often explored in Renaissance art. This expressive drawing, rendered in pen, black ink, and gray wash, showcases the artist's masterful draftsmanship and use of light and shadow.
items.tags: biblical, religious, renaissance, venetian, drawing, narrative, spiritual, ink wash

items.title: The Submersion of Pharaoh's Army in the Red Sea
items.medium: Woodcut in black on ivory laid paper
items.description_narrative: Titian's monumental woodcut vividly depicts the dramatic destruction of Pharaoh's army as they pursue the Israelites through the parting Red Sea. The composition showcases the artist's mastery in rendering intense action and emotional turmoil through the medium of black ink on paper.
items.tags: religious, biblical, destruction, woodcut, printmaking, renaissance, dramatic, Venetian

items.title: Self-Portrait
items.medium: Black chalk, with stumping, on gray wove paper, tipped on to ivory laid paper
items.description_narrative: This self-portrait by Titian offers a direct and intimate depiction of the artist. Rendered in black chalk with stumping, the drawing highlights the artist's masterful draftsmanship.
items.tags: self-portrait, portrait, chalk drawing, renaissance, venetian, master, artist's gaze

items.title: Penitent Magdalene
items.medium: Red chalk, with stumping, on ivory laid paper
items.description_narrative: This striking drawing depicts Mary Magdalene, a figure often associated with repentance and devotion in Christian art. Executed in red chalk with stumping on ivory laid paper, it highlights the textural qualities of the medium.
items.tags: mary magdalene, religious, drawing, red chalk, devotional, repentance, figure study

items.title: Portrait of a Lady
items.description_narrative: This oil on canvas depicts a dignified lady, rendered with the rich colors and subtle modeling characteristic of Venetian Renaissance portraiture. Created around 1550, it reflects the artistic style of Titian's workshop or a close follower.
items.tags: portrait, oil painting, renaissance, lady, venetian art, sixteenth century

items.title: Scenes from the Life of Saint John the Baptist
items.description_narrative: This tempera on panel artwork, 'Scenes from the Life of Saint John the Baptist,' was created by Bartolomeo di Giovanni. Dating from around 1490–95, it vividly depicts significant moments from the saint's life.
items.tags: religious, narrative, early renaissance, italian, tempera, saint john the baptist

items.title: Cupid Chastised
items.description_narrative: Bartolomeo Manfredi's "Cupid Chastised" depicts a mythological scene centered on the punishment of the god of love. Executed in oil on canvas, the work showcases the dramatic light and shadow characteristic of the artist's era.
items.tags: mythology, cupid, baroque, caravaggism, italian, oil painting, dramatic

items.title: The Nativity
items.description_narrative: Fra Bartolommeo's 'The Nativity' depicts the birth of Jesus Christ, a central event in Christian theology. This oil on panel painting showcases the artist's High Renaissance style and devotion.
items.tags: nativity, religious art, christianity, renaissance, high renaissance, italian art, sacred, oil painting

items.title: The Crucifixion
items.description_narrative: Francisco de Zurbarán's 1627 oil on canvas, 'The Crucifixion,' presents a singular, stark depiction of Christ on the cross. The painting is characterized by its dramatic use of light and shadow, emphasizing the figure's isolation and the solemnity of the moment.
items.tags: crucifixion, religious art, Spanish Baroque, realism, tenebrism, devotional, dramatic

items.title: Alessandro de' Medici
items.description_narrative: Pontormo's oil on panel portrait captures Alessandro de' Medici, Duke of Florence, with a penetrating gaze, reflecting his powerful status. This work exemplifies the distinctive Mannerist style prevalent in the mid-16th century Italian Renaissance.
items.tags: portrait, mannerism, italian renaissance, medici, nobility, oil painting, 16th century

items.title: Christ Carrying the Cross
items.description_narrative: Sebastiano del Piombo captures the dramatic moment of Christ carrying the cross towards his crucifixion, a powerful depiction of suffering and resolve. This oil on panel painting by Sebastiano del Piombo vividly portrays Christ's arduous journey, highlighting the profound emotional weight of the event.
items.tags: christ, crucifixion, religious art, high renaissance, italian, suffering, dramatic, oil painting

items.title: The Crucifixion
items.description_narrative: Carlo Crivelli's 'The Crucifixion', painted around 1487, depicts the central Christian narrative with his characteristic tempera on panel technique. This work exemplifies his meticulous detail and expressive figural style, typical of the late 15th century.
items.tags: religious, renaissance, tempera, italian, biblical, narrative, devotional, early renaissance

items.title: Fragment
items.medium: Silk and gilt-animal-substrate-wrapped linen, warp-float faced 3:1 twill weave with supplementary patterning wefts bound by secondary binding warps in (weft-float faced 1:3) twill interlacings (on reverse face secondary binding warps and supplementary wefts form detached interlacing)
items.description_narrative: This intricate textile fragment from the late 14th or 15th century showcases sophisticated weaving techniques. It features silk and gilt-animal-substrate-wrapped linen, utilizing a complex warp-float faced twill weave with supplementary patterning wefts.
items.tags: textile, silk, medieval, fragment, decorative, weaving, gilt

items.title: Saint John the Baptist Entering the Wilderness
items.description_narrative: Giovanni di Paolo depicts Saint John the Baptist embarking on his spiritual journey into the wilderness in this tempera on panel painting. The artwork showcases the artist's distinctive style, characterized by its vibrant color and intricate narrative detail.
items.tags: religious, early renaissance, sienese school, tempera, narrative, spiritual, wilderness

items.title: Ecce Agnus Dei
items.description_narrative: Giovanni di Paolo's 'Ecce Agnus Dei' depicts John the Baptist gesturing towards Jesus Christ, emphasizing Christ's role as the Lamb of God. This tempera on panel painting exemplifies the distinct narrative and spiritual intensity of Sienese art.
items.tags: religious, biblical, sienese, quattrocento, tempera, italian, devotional, early renaissance

items.title: The Assassination and Funeral of Julius Caesar
items.medium: Tempera on panel, transferred to canvas mounted on pressed hardboard and cradled
items.description_narrative: This painting vividly depicts the dramatic assassination and subsequent funeral of Julius Caesar, a pivotal event in Roman history. Created by the Workshop of Apollonio di Giovanni, this tempera on panel artwork captures the narrative intensity of these historical moments.
items.tags: roman history, julius caesar, assassination, funeral, renaissance, italian art, narrative, historical

items.title: The Garden of Paradise
items.description_narrative: This oil on panel artwork, 'The Garden of Paradise,' emerges from the workshop of Hieronymus Bosch. It presents a fantastical and allegorical vision typical of the artist's distinctive style.
items.tags: religious art, northern renaissance, fantasy, allegorical, netherlandish, oil painting, workshop production

items.title: The Adventures of Ulysses
items.description_narrative: This tempera on panel painting illustrates scenes from Homer's Odyssey, chronicling the epic journey of the hero Ulysses. Created during the early 15th century, it brings to life tales of ancient mythology.
items.tags: mythology, epic, ancient greece, early renaissance, narrative, italian, tempera

items.title: The Last Communion of Saint Jerome
items.description_narrative: Botticelli's 'The Last Communion of Saint Jerome' depicts the aged saint receiving his final communion before death, a poignant moment of devotion. Rendered in tempera and gold on wood, this painting exemplifies the meticulous craftsmanship characteristic of its era.
items.tags: religious, devotional, christian, saint jerome, renaissance, italian, tempera

items.title: The Annunciation
items.description_narrative: Botticelli's 'The Annunciation' depicts the pivotal biblical moment when the Archangel Gabriel announces to Mary that she will conceive the Son of God. Rendered with tempera and gold on wood, this work exemplifies the luminous artistry of the Early Renaissance.
items.tags: annunciation, religious, christian art, renaissance, italian, tempera, devotional
